raw.author: thegarybrecka
raw.text:
Your weight problem might actually be a liver problem. Most people think their liver is just responsible for detoxification, but it plays a major role in how your body processes fat, regulates blood sugar, and responds to insulin.

When fat starts building up in your liver, it can contribute to insulin resistance, inflammation, and disrupted metabolic signaling, making weight management even more difficult.

If you're struggling to lose weight, it's time to look beyond the scale and start paying attention to your metabolic health.

A CGM SHOWS THE PROBLEM. 
CUTTING CARBS FIXES IT.

NEJM's new CONNECT trial found a continuous glucose monitor helped people with type 2 diabetes lower their A1c. Good. Watching your sugar in real time is a wake-up call.

But a monitor only tells you what the food did. In a 1-year study of a low-carb, ketogenic approach, 262 people with type 2 diabetes dropped their average A1c from 7.6% to 6.3%. Insulin was cut back or stopped in 94% of the people taking it.

That study wasn't randomized, but those are results most diabetes clinics never see.

raw.author: OwenGregorian
raw.text:
Tiny injectable glucose sensor could make blood sugar monitoring 10 times cheaper | Rachit Agarwal, Digital Trends

Continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) have saved a lot of people from pricking their fingers several times a day. They are still far from perfect, and cost a lot. A team at Texas A&M University thinks it has a cheaper and simpler alternative. In a study published in ACS Measurement Science Au, the researchers describe a sensor small enough to inject under your skin.

Why do current glucose monitors still feel like a chore?

A typical CGM has a thin sensor under your skin and a patch on top holding it in place. You swap it out every 5 to 14 days, and the adhesive can leave your skin red and itchy over time. Many models also need calibration with finger-prick readings, which defeats part of the purpose. A single sensor costs anywhere from about $60 to $180, and without decent insurance, that bill keeps coming back.

So, how does a glowing sugar molecule measure glucose?

The Texas A&M sensor doesn’t use enzymes at all. It relies on a protein that latches onto sugar and a near-infrared dye attached to a sugar molecule. When your glucose climbs, glucose kicks the dye-tagged molecule loose, and its glow changes. Near-infrared light travels through skin well, so a reader outside your body could pick up the signal without any electronics inside the implant. The researchers also believe it could work regardless of your skin tone.

What I like most is the focus on cost. The team chose a sugar molecule called beta-mannopentaose, which is roughly 10 times cheaper than the version it was compared against, and it held up just as well. In lab tests, it tracked glucose between 25 and 400 mg/dL, which covers low, normal, and high readings.

All of this fits inside a hydrogel rod about 2.5mm wide and 11mm long, designed to be injected under the skin. After seven days, the rod still held more than 94% of the glowing sugar molecule.

When can you actually get one?

Nobody can say yet. The sensor has only been tested in the lab, and the researchers still have to show it works reliably inside the body for long stretches. If they pull it off, a patch-free monitor at a fraction of today’s price would make a real difference for the more than 500 million people living with diabetes.

https://t.co/O9R2TOLnvl

如何判断自己或者自己的孩子是否已经胰岛素抵抗了？Dr. Boz提及了四种胰岛素抵抗迹象： 

1） 带小“颈”的皮肤赘生物（腋窝、腹股沟、颈部）。
2） 颈后及褶皱处皮肤呈深色、厚实、丝绒状 → 黑棘皮病。看起来像永久性污垢。
3） 脚趾、脚踝和小腿的毛发逐渐消失。
4） 过早出现白发和加速衰老。  

记住，这些症状都可以通过生酮饮食逆转！
关注我，了解更多生酮自愈路径！
